Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:165446
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 35013 of 2023

Applicant :- Sanjay
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Anand Pati Tiwari,Deepak Upadhyay
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Awadhesh Kumar Pandey
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Sri Chandra Kumar Singh, Advocate submits that on 10.08.2023 he has filed his power on behalf
of the informant in the office of this Court but his name is not shown in the cause list but he is ready
to argue.

2. Heard Sri Anand Pati Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Chandra Kumar Singh,
learned counsel for the informant and Sri Jhamman Ram, learned AGA for the State.

3. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 238 of 2023, under Sections 363, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Jahangirabad, District Bulandshahar during pendency of the trial.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant under Section 363 IPC and according to the FIR applicant abducted the daughter of the informant aged about 13 years.

entities.text: Sanjay vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and on record there are three statements of the proseuctrix.

The first was recorded before the Investigating Officer and second was recorded before the CWC and the third one was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and in all the three statements she narrated different stories.

He further submits that in the second statement, she categorically stated that she loved the applicant for three years and when her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded then she categorically stated that applicant never committed rape with her.

6. He further submits that actually prosecutrix wanted to perform marriage with the applicant but her parents was not ready to perform her marriage with the applicant and they settled her marriage with some other person and only due to this reason she according to her own wish had left her paternal home.
He further submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 17.05.2023.

7. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. prosecutrix categorically stated that no physical relationship was developed between applicant and her and she also did not state that applicant kidnapped her.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Considering the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant - Sanjay be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
12.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
